comparisonScope.description: Complete declared Task Board replication scope: fixed 1280×800 CSS-pixel viewport; rendered interface properties and states; create, complete, filter, delete, keyboard, validation, and API success/failure behavior at a deterministic in-memory adapter boundary.
conditions: Fresh in-memory task store for each run
Same input title: Prepare release notes
Fresh client page and deterministic in-memory API route adapter
excludedDimensions: Production network transport and server behavior

operations.method: Map implementation-local node identifiers by parent path and node role

alignments.rationale: Both observations are initial empty-state snapshots for the same Task Board subject and viewport.
Both observations exercise the same create/complete/filter/delete sequence with the same input.
Both records are the POST /api/tasks exchange for the same input at the same deterministic adapter boundary.
Both captures cover the same declared UI properties and state sequence under the same browser and viewport conditions.
Both captures execute the same pointer and keyboard workflows, validation cases, and rejected-request scenario.
Both captures retain the same eight API events, including successful POST/PATCH/DELETE exchanges and a rejected POST with HTTP 503.

results.reason: The captured main container geometry is identical at the shared viewport.
The mutated implementation was executed in Chromium and displayed '1 tasks' after creating one task; the reference displayed '1 task'. This is a directly observed mismatch.
For their respective inputs, both adapters returned HTTP 200 and initialized completed=false. Input-specific title values are excluded from this comparison.
The deliberately mutated build renders the plural label for a singular task; the retained 1280×800 screenshots differ by 272 pixels.
Keyboard activation and state transitions work, but the deliberate singular/plural mutation is also observable in the keyboard workflow summary.
Both implementations block empty required input and ignore whitespace-only input without issuing API requests.
The full deterministic adapter request/response traces and rejected-request runtime error outcomes agree.

limitations: Two required properties remain partial: font rendering beyond the recorded Chromium/Linux environment and the maximum title-length boundary.
Two optional properties remain explicitly excluded and one property is not applicable within the Task Board fixture.
The reference and independent baseline are pixel-identical in 13 tested states, including three responsive widths, focus, hover, and dark colour-scheme preference.
The security result covers only the tested HTML/SVG/script-shaped task-title payloads; it is not a general security assessment.

The API is a deterministic in-memory adapter, not a production service; persistence, messaging, identity, authorization, background processing, integrations, and application configuration are outside this target boundary.
Performance values are single-run hosted-CI navigation samples, not production benchmarks or SLO evidence.

conclusion.statement: The deliberately mutated implementation still differs in singular/plural task summary (272 differing pixels in the one-active state). The reference and independent baseline match pixel-for-pixel in all 13 tested UI states, and agree on the expanded behaviour, title, data, HTTP 503 failure, and limited output-encoding probes. Performance samples are recorded but treated as incomparable single-run measurements. Both captures remain incomplete.

Two required properties remain partial: font rendering beyond the recorded Chromium/Linux environment and the maximum title-length boundary.
